meta.tagline: Wood-fired Roman cooking in the heart of Oakland

sections.headline: Roman classics, cooked over fire
sections.subheadline: Hand-rolled pasta, blistered pizza, and a short list of Italian wines poured by people who drink them.

items.title: Pasta made daily
items.description: Every shape is rolled and cut in-house each morning, then finished to order in the pan.

items.title: Wood-fired oven
items.description: Our oven runs at 850F on almond and oak, which gives the crust its char and chew.

items.title: Small-grower wine list
items.description: Thirty bottles from family estates across Lazio, Piedmont, and Sicily, most under 60 dollars.

items.title: Walk-ins welcome
items.description: Half the dining room and the full bar are held back for guests without a reservation.

sections.heading: Our kitchen
sections.body: Trattoria Nove opened in 2016 in a former hardware store on Grand Avenue. Chef Lucia Fanelli grew up cooking in her grandmother's kitchen outside Rome, and the menu still leans on those recipes: cacio e pepe finished with pasta water and nothing else, artichokes fried twice, saltimbocca with sage cut from the planter by the back door. We buy produce from four Bay Area farms, mill our own semolina blend, and change the menu when the market changes rather than on a schedule. The dining room seats forty-eight, the bar seats ten, and the kitchen is open so you can watch the oven work.

items.quote: The cacio e pepe is the best version I have eaten outside of Trastevere, and the room feels like a neighborhood place rather than a destination.
items.author: Dana Whitfield

items.quote: We booked for six on a Tuesday and left three hours later having ordered half the menu twice. The service never rushed us once.
items.author: Marcus Oyelaran

items.quote: Lucia sent out fried artichokes we did not order because the delivery had just arrived. That is the whole restaurant in one gesture.
items.author: Priya Raghavan

sections.headline: What we are cooking this week
sections.subheadline: The menu shifts with the market, so treat this as a snapshot rather than a promise.

items.title: Antipasti
items.description: Twice-fried artichokes, whipped ricotta with honey, marinated anchovies, and a rotating salumi board.

items.title: Pasta
items.description: Cacio e pepe, rigatoni all'amatriciana, cassarecce with lamb ragu, and a vegetarian shape that changes weekly.

items.title: Pizza
items.description: Margherita, salsiccia with broccoli rabe, and a white pie with potato, rosemary, and taleggio.

items.title: Dolci
items.description: Olive oil cake, affogato with our own espresso, and a torta della nonna baked each afternoon.

items.question: Can you cook gluten-free pasta?
items.answer: Yes. We keep a dedicated pot and strainer for gluten-free shapes, though the wood oven is shared and we cannot promise a fully gluten-free kitchen.

items.question: Are there vegan options?
items.answer: Every night has at least one vegan antipasto, one vegan pasta, and a marinara pizza. Tell your server and the kitchen will build a full vegan menu for the table.

items.question: Do you have a kids menu?
items.answer: No separate menu, but the kitchen will happily make a half portion of buttered pasta or a plain margherita for younger guests.

items.question: Is there a corkage fee?
items.answer: Twenty-five dollars per bottle, waived on Mondays and limited to two bottles per table.

items.title: Tuesday to Thursday
items.description: Dinner from 5:30pm to 9:30pm, with the bar open until 10:30pm.

items.title: Friday and Saturday
items.description: Dinner from 5:00pm to 10:30pm, and the bar stays open until midnight.

items.title: Sunday
items.description: Family-style supper from 4:00pm to 8:30pm, one seating menu at 55 dollars per person.

items.title: Monday
items.description: Closed, except for private events booked through our events team.
